text:
Government’s excuse for non-implementation of schemes
In continuation of the lies to hoodwink the people of the State, the Finance Minister suggests that given the greater share of salaries and pensions in the State’s own revenues, the State Government is unable to implement the programmes. The Finance Minister tries to mislead the people into believing that this resulted from the policies of the previous YSRCP Government. However, the truth is, even in 2019-20, the first year of YSRCP Government, the share was way higher as 84.71%, when compared with the first year of the TDP alliance Government. Added to that, there was Covid-19 pandemic and despite that, the then Government did not find excuses to implement the election commitments.

text:
Details of debt
The details of debt along with estimated debt figures for the next year has, as a tradition, been a part of the Budget in brief (Volume VI).

This time, very conveniently the Government avoided the table. The reason is quite apparent. The intent is that, if this table is made part of the budget in brief, then the lies of the Government regarding the 10 lakh crore debt would be exposed. 

The figures as of 31st March, 2024 are extracted from Volume V of the budget documents. To the same, adjustments are made to account for further receipts and disbursements under the heads ‘6003’, ‘6004’ aggregating to public debt as contained in Volumes II and III/5 of budget volumes and public account as contained in Volume IV.

text:
Allocation for capital city
In the demand for grants placed before the Legislative Assembly for Municipal Administration and Urban Development, an amount of Rs. 6,000 crores was shown as an allocation for Amaravati Capital City Development. The budget speech of the finance minister describes the project as a self sustaining one. The budget allocation for a self sustaining project was subsequently viewed by the Government as a logic defying proposition and to address this, they had once again tried to blatantly mislead the public by conveying that this Rs. 6,000 crores is not for capital city development but for yearly pensions to land owners. 
Rs. 6,000 crores has been allocated under the head 4215-01-051-03-80-530-531. This is shown under Construction head. 







The amount to land owners as annuity is Rs. 297.82 crores and the same has been allocated under the head 4215-01-050-11-05-530-532








Is the Government’s fact check on the matter, wrong (or) is the demand for grants made as per the Constitution of India, wrong? 
The Government should clarify.

text:
Growth estimated in FY 2025-26
Note – The budget for FY 2025-26 estimates a growth of 25.63% in State’s own revenues in year FY 26. Going by the 10 month performance during FY 25, one can estimate the State’s own revenues during FY 25 would be able to reach Rs. 93,500 crores by the year end, with great difficulty. In FY 2025-26, it is estimated that Rs. 1,28,126 crores would be received as own revenues. That is a growth of 37% or around Rs. 35,000 crores. Is this possible?

If this increase in revenues is not achieved, then to that extent, Government will have to borrow or cut down expenditure.
What is the State Government’s plan?

Is this part of the State Government’s plan to deceive the people or is there any agenda of the Government to  burden the people with some new strategy?

State economic performance in a nutshell
- The above table provides ample clarity about the way in which, the current dispensation deceives the people. In the first 10 months of this financial year 2024-25, own revenues shrunk by 0.01% and capital expenditure reduced by a huge 48.17%. When facts stood thus, the Government projects that in FY 2024-25 as per revised estimates, own revenues grow at 9.56%, capital expenditure grows at 3.18% and that the GSDP grows at 12.94%. A glance at the performance in the first 10 months draws everyone’s attention to the fact that the estimates of the Government are far from reality. 

On these already inflated figures for FY 2024-25, the Government projects significant growth in FY 2025-26, leading to unjustifiable budget estimates
